L80:   * 【1†Español】
L81: ## Overview
L82: 
L83: Car seats and booster seats provide protection for infants and children in a crash, yet car crashes are a leading cause of death for children ages 1 to 13. It's important to choose the right seat and use it correctly every time your child is in the car.  Follow these important steps to choose the right car seat or booster seat, install it correctly and know when it’s safe for your kid to transition to a seat belt.

L120: # The Process
L121: 
L122: Follow these steps to help you through the process of finding the right car seat, installing it correctly, and keeping your child safe.
L123: 
L124: ### Find the right car seat
L125:

L127:   * Learn about the four 【55†car seat types】
L128:   * 【50†Find and compare car seats】 and ease-of-use-ratings using NHTSA’s Car Seat Finder
L129: ### Install your car seat correctly

L133:   * Get your 【58†car seat inspected】 at a station nearest you

L142: # Car Seat Overview
L143:

L148: 【59†Car Seat Recommendations】
L149: 
L150: There are many car seat choices on the market. Use the information below to help you choose the type of car seat that best meets your child’s needs:
L151:   * Select a car seat based on your child’s age and size, then choose a seat that fits in your vehicle, and use it every time.
L152:   * Always refer to your specific car seat manufacturer’s instructions (check height and weight limits) and read the vehicle owner’s manual on how to install the car seat using the seat belt or lower anchors and a tether, if available.
L153:   * To maximize safety, keep your child in the car seat for as long as possible, as long as the child fits within the manufacturer’s height and weight requirements.
L154:   * Keep your child in the back seat at least through age 12.
L155: ### Recommended car seats based on your child's age and size
L156: 
L157: 【60†Image】
L158: 
L159: Find The Right Car Seat
L160: 
L161: # Types and Recommendations
L162: 
L163: ### Rear-Facing Car Seat
L164: 
L165: 【61†Image: Car seat rear-facing】
L166: 
L167: The best seat for your young child to use. It has a harness and, in a crash, cradles and moves with your child to reduce the stress to the child's fragile neck and spinal cord. Find out 【62†how to install rear-facing car seats】.
L168: #### Birth-12 Months
L169: 
L170: Your child under age 1 should always ride in a rear-facing car seat. There are different types of rear-facing car seats:
L171: 
L172:   * Infant-only seats can only be used rear-facing.
L173:   * Convertible and all-in-one car seats typically have higher height and weight limits for the rear-facing position, allowing you to keep your child rear-facing for a longer period of time.
L174: #### 1 – 3 Years
L175: 
L176: Keep your child rear-facing as long as possible. It’s the best way to keep him or her safe. Your child should remain in a rear-facing car seat until he or she reaches the top height or weight limit allowed by your car seat’s manufacturer. Once your child outgrows the rear-facing car seat, your child is ready to travel in a forward-facing car seat with a harness and tether.
L177: ### Forward-Facing Car Seat
L178: 
L179: 【63†Image: Car seat forward-facing】
L180: 
L181: Has a harness and tether that limits your child's forward movement during a crash. Find out 【64†how to install forward-facing car seats】.
L182: #### 1 – 3 Years
L183: 
L184: Keep your child rear-facing as long as possible. It’s the best way to keep him or her safe. Your child should remain in a rear-facing car seat until he or she reaches the top height or weight limit allowed by your car seat’s manufacturer. Once your child outgrows the rear-facing car seat, your child is ready to travel in a forward-facing car seat with a harness and tether.
L185: #### 4 – 7 Years
L186: 
L187: Keep your child in a forward-facing car seat with a harness and tether until he or she reaches the top height or weight limit allowed by your car seat’s manufacturer. Once your child outgrows the forward-facing car seat with a harness, it’s time to travel in a booster seat, but still in the back seat.
L188: ### Booster Seat
L189: 
L190: 【65†Image: Car seat booster】
L191: 
L192: Raises and positions a child so the vehicle’s lap-and-shoulder belt fits properly over the stronger points of a child’s body, the hips and across the chest. Find out 【66†how to install a booster seat】.
L193: #### 4 – 7 Years
L194: 
L195: Keep your child in a forward-facing car seat with a harness and tether until he or she reaches the top height or weight limit allowed by your car seat’s manufacturer. Once your child outgrows the forward-facing car seat with a harness, it’s time to travel in a booster seat, but still in the back seat.
L196: #### 8 – 12 Years
L197: 
L198: Keep your child in a booster seat until he or she is big enough to fit in a seat belt properly. For a seat belt to fit properly the lap belt must lie snugly across the upper thighs, not the stomach. The shoulder belt should lie snugly across the shoulder and chest and not cross the neck or face. Remember: your child should still ride in the back seat because it’s safer there.
L199: 
L200: ### Seat Belt
L201: 
L202: 【67†Image: Seat Belt】
L203: #### 8 – 12 Years

For a seat belt to fit properly the lap belt must lie snugly across the upper thighs, not the stomach. The shoulder belt should lie snugly across the shoulder and chest and not cross the neck or face. Remember: your child should still ride in the back seat because it’s safer there.

L219: The Car Seat Finder is an easy-to-use tool that lets you compare seats and 【69†ease-of-use ratings】 to find the right car seat for your child. L223: Installation Help
L224: # Car Seat Installation Parts and Tips
L225: Your child’s safety could be in jeopardy if your car seat is not installed correctly. Not all car seats fit in all vehicles. Make sure the car seat is 【70†the right fit for your vehicle†chrome-extension】 (PDF, 1.77 MB). Test the car seat you plan to buy to make sure it fits well in your vehicle. Before you install your car seat, make sure you’re familiar with vehicle and car seat parts used in the installation process and these 【71†important installation safety tips】.
L226: ## Vehicle and Car Seat Parts Explained
L227: Every car seat needs to be installed using either the lower anchors or a seat belt to secure it in place, never both. If you choose to use a seat belt to install your car seat, pay close attention to how to  “lock” your seat belt according to the vehicle’s owner manual. With a forward-facing car seat, use a tether if one is available. Before installing your car seat make sure you understand the function and location of the vehicle and car seat parts that are used in installation.
L228: 
L229: 【72†Car Seat Glossary】
L230: ### Vehicle Parts
L231: 
L232: #### Lower Anchors
L233: 
L234: Used for installing a car seat using its lower anchor attachments
L235: 
L236: The lower anchors are found in a minimum of two rear seating positions in a vehicle. Each lower-anchor-equipped seating position has two small horizontal bars found in the space between the vehicle seat’s back and bottom cushion (the “seat bight”).
L237: #### Tether Anchor
L238: 
L239: Used for attaching a car seat's tether to the vehicle
L240: 
L241: Typically there are a minimum of three tether anchors in a vehicle. In sedans, these are usually located above/behind the vehicle’s back seat on the rear shelf. In some larger vehicles such as vans, pickup trucks, and SUVs, these tether anchors may be found on the back of a vehicle seat, on the floor, the ceiling, or other location.
L242: To avoid confusing tether anchors with other hardware such as luggage tie-downs, be sure to read your vehicle’s owner manual carefully to find out where they are located in your particular vehicle.
L243: ### Car Seat Parts
L244: 
L245: 【73†Image】
L246: 
L247: 
L248: 
L249: ##### Attach top tether from the car seat to the tether anchor in the vehicle.
L250: 
L251: ##### Fasten lower anchor attachments on the car seat to the lower anchors in the vehicle.
L252: 
L253: #### Lower Anchor Attachments
L254: 
L255: Used to install the car seat in a vehicle with lower anchors
L256: #### Tether
L257: 
L258: Used to secure a forward-facing car seat and limit forward head movement in a crash
L259: The tether is located on the top rear of convertible, combination, and all-in-one car seats. It’s adjustable and has a hook and strap that connects to one of your vehicle’s tether anchors. Most rear-facing car seats in the United States do not use a tether for installation. However, installations vary from model to model, so you must review your particular car seat’s instructions and your vehicle’s owner manual carefully.
L260: Follow your car seat manufacturer’s instructions regarding when and how to use the tether for your particular seat. NHTSA recommends always using a tether with a forward-facing car seat—installed with your vehicle’s seat belt OR the lower anchors—as long as it is permitted by both the car seat and vehicle manufacturers. IMPORTANT: Both installation methods are designed to work with the tether to achieve the highest level of safety for child passengers restrained in forward-facing car seats.
L261: ### Lower Anchor Weight Limits
L262: 
L263: Lower anchors have weight limits set by the vehicle and car seat manufacturers. You can determine the lower anchor weight limit by checking the warning label or installation diagrams located on the side of the car seat. If your car seat does not have a label, you can determine the maximum allowable child weight for lower anchor use by subtracting the weight of the car seat (usually available in the car seat’s instruction manual) from 65 pounds.
L264: Lower anchor weight limit = 65 lbs – weight of car seat
L265: #### Know the Facts
L266: 
L267: Once your child outgrows the vehicle or car seat manufacturer’s established limits for the lower anchors, stop using the lower anchor attachments and reinstall the car seat using the vehicle’s seat belt.

L280: # Car Seat Inspection
L281: ### Get your car seat inspected
L282: 
L283: Whether you’ve just installed a car seat or need help installing or using one, get help at a car seat inspection station near you. Certified technicians will inspect your car seat free of charge, in most cases, and show you how to correctly install and use it. Some locations now offer virtual inspections.

L287: Can’t find an inspection station near you? You may be able to find a tech through 【74†Safe Kids Worldwide†portalskcms.cyzap.net】.

L289: Registration
L290: # Register Your Car Seat
L291: 
L292: Congratulations — you chose the right car seat and installed it correctly. Now it’s time to register your car seat with the manufacturer to receive recalls and safety notices so your child can remain safe. Also, you can sign up with NHTSA to receive e-mail alerts about car seat and booster seat recalls.
L293:

L296: # Register your car seat to receive important safety updates
L297: #### Registering your car seat makes sense
L298: 
L299: The car seat manufacturer can contact you directly about recalls and safety notices.
L300: #### Registering your car seat is easy
L301: 
L302: Send in the card that came with your car seat or complete a quick registration on the manufacturer’s website. Your child’s safety could depend on it.
L303: 
L304: [Select] Go to Website
L305: 
L306: Need help?
L307: 
L308: If you are unable to register your child’s seat with the manufacturer, contact NHTSA at NHTSA.ODI.ced@dot.gov.
L309: 
L310: Also, get recall notices from NHTSA
L311: In addition to registering your car seat to receive recalls and safety notices from your car seat manufacturer, you can download our 【75†SaferCar App】 for free to get alerts on your mobile device about car seat and booster seat recalls. You can also 【76†sign up to receive e-mail alerts】.
